entries.comment: Samus: Samus's reputation: how troopers, Pirates, hunters and the Federation see her
entries.content:
Samus Aran is famous across the galaxy and known to almost no one. Per the original manual she was "the greatest of all the space hunters", credited with missions "everybody thought were absolutely impossible", yet her "true form is shrouded in mystery."

- Galactic Federation leadership: it hires her for what its own forces cannot do: Zebes, when the Federation Police turned to a space hunter as a last resort; Fleet Admiral Castor Dane's call to clear a virus from the Aurora Units; ZDR after its E.M.M.I. went silent. The trust has limits (see Samus's defiance of the Federation at the BSL).
- Marines and troopers: mostly awe. On Tanamaar, soldiers ambushed by Space Pirates called out "It's Samus. She's punching through" and "I can't believe it. It's Samus. It's really her." Private Nora Armstrong admires her as a role model for her "famously unshakable demeanor"; Myles MacKenzie introduced her to a wrecked battle mech with "You know her. She's... she's famous." The stories are mess-hall talk: when Bravo Squad's M. Angseth, who wished she were in the field like Samus, told how one bounty hunter blew up a planet full of Space Pirates, PFC I. Crany dismissed it as "fairy tales", lumping "this Samus" with "Bigfoot, or Santa Claus." On the Bottle Ship the 07th Platoon received her warily; only Anthony Higgs greeted her as an old friend ("Fancy meeting you here, Princess").
- Space Pirates: to them she is "the Hunter", "the accursed Hunter, Samus Aran", a priority target with a bounty on her head (see The Pirates and Samus (the Hunter)).
- Fellow bounty hunters: respect laced with rivalry. Rundas, Ghor and Gandrayda fought beside her on Norion. Federation intel noted that Gandrayda saw "the veteran Hunter Samus Aran as her chief rival"; once corrupted, Pirate records say she "vowed to present Aran's bloody helmet to Dark Samus as tribute." A Federation briefing presumed hostile the six hunters who raced her for the Alimbic power, and Sylux hates her outright.
- Prophecy and hope: the Chozo of Tallon IV foretold an Entrusted One and wondered whether the Newborn, the child they had found long ago, was the one their seers spoke of; the Lamorn hailed her as their Chosen One; the Luminoth had no prophecy, but U-Mos told her plainly, "You're our only hope, Samus."

The legend runs ahead of the woman: strangers expect the hero of the stories, or doubt she exists, and meet a taciturn professional.
entries.notes: Quotes checked against primary transcriptions: original-manual lines (metroiddatabase; the manual's 'he/his' paraphrased away; 'last resort' was the Federation Police's decision); Tanamaar soldiers' and Myles's lines (Shinesparkers Prime 4 transcript; the soldiers are unnamed and were ambushed, and Myles is speaking to the wrecked MK-99 Betsy); Nora's 'famously unshakable demeanor' (Biology logbook via OmegaMetroid); Angseth's wish to be in the field like Samus, Crany's account that Angseth told of a bounty hunter who 'blew up a planet full of Space Pirates', 'fairy tales' and 'this Samus, or Bigfoot, or Santa Claus' (Echoes trooper logs, re-read on Metroid Wiki Trooper Logs); 'accursed Hunter, Samus Aran' (Corruption Pirate Data); Gandrayda's Federation data and Pirate 'bloody helmet' log; 'Disposition of rival interests is presumed hostile' (Hunters). Fixes from fact-check: the Dane mission was changed from 'carry the vaccine' (unconfirmed by Metroid Wiki or Wikipedia) to Wikipedia's 'clear a virus from ... Aurora Units'; 'pinned down' became 'ambushed'; the Prophecy bullet became 'Prophecy and hope', the Tallon IV Chozo 'wondered whether the Newborn' was the Defender rather than 'foretold her', and U-Mos's line is framed as a plea; Angseth's admiration was added to balance Crany. The 07th Platoon's wary reception rests on the existing Other M entries (Anthony 'the only member who treated Samus amicably from the start'); his greeting quote is the one already in Other M: Anthony Higgs. Unverified 'raised guns' and Adam's join-under-orders details were not added. Keys: generic 'heard of you', 'heard about you', 'your reputation', 'her reputation' and 'it's really her' were dropped; all remaining keys are Samus-specific multi-word phrases, so no secondary gating is needed. The phrase 'the most famous hunter of her time' is untraceable to an official source and is not used. Kept to one clause each where other entries go deeper (Fusion defiance, Pirate logs, hunter bios, Sylux, Bravo Squad). No game titles in content.

entries.content:
Humans are the species Samus Aran was born into and the backbone of the Galactic Federation's military, research and colonies, though not its only people: the Federation hires non-human bounty hunters such as Rundas and Gandrayda, and per the manga her Federation Police comrades Kreatz and Mauk were not human (see Kreatz and Mauk). The Federation Marine Corps is predominantly human, as are many of the people Samus has served and worked beside: her former commander Adam Malkovich, her old comrade Anthony Higgs, Fleet Admiral Castor Dane and the Bottle Ship scientist Madeline Bergman. Humans crew Federation outposts such as Norion, and no other sapient species appears as often in her missions.

Earth is, by every indication, humanity's homeworld. Per the original manual, the Federation researchers who discovered the Metroid on SR388 were bringing it back to Earth when Space Pirates seized it, and per the manga Samus's birthplace, K-2L, was an Earth colony (see K-2L (Samus's home colony)). Federation warships such as the Olympus, the Valhalla, the Tyr and the Theseus carry names from Earth myth. When Earth joined the Federation is not recorded, nor is the location of Federation Headquarters (see Daiban and Federation Headquarters), and no mission record places Samus on Earth.

Samus is human by birth, but not only human: the Chozo gave her their DNA (at age three, per the manga), and the vaccine that saved her from the X gave her Metroid DNA (see Samus Aran – Metroid DNA, Chozo DNA and what she has become). Raised by the Chozo on Zebes, she rejoined human society when she enlisted with the Federation. Asked "are you human?", the accurate answer is: by birth, yes; by blood, not only.
entries.notes: Fixes from fact-check: dropped Myles MacKenzie and the Viewros castaways (no source gives their species, and VUE-995 is an android); 'Earth is humanity's homeworld' now hedged ('by every indication'), since Metroid Wiki's Human page says only 'presumably originating on the planet Earth'; the ship naming was toned down to an observation ('carry names from Earth myth'; the source is Metroid Wiki etymology trivia) and 'Its old stories travel with the Federation' removed; the age-three DNA detail is labelled per the manga; Norion reworded to 'Humans crew Federation outposts such as Norion' (infobox race=Humans only). Added non-human Federation people: Rundas and Gandrayda, bounty hunters taking Federation orders (Wikipedia Corruption plot), and Kreatz and Mauk. Metroid Wiki's Human page states they were 'Federation troopers of alien-to-Earth species'. A search snippet (Wikitroid mirror) corroborates Mauk's non-human race (heightened sense of smell, a race recommended for Federation membership). The existing Manga: Kreatz and Mauk entry says their species is not recorded, so that entry may want a one-clause update. Keys: bare 'Earth' was replaced by phrases ('planet Earth', 'from Earth', 'Earth's', 'visit Earth') to avoid idioms like 'what on Earth' and 'down to earth'. Secondaries dropped the near-universal 'Metroid', 'galaxy' and 'DNA' and added 'homeworld', 'born' and 'alien'. Bare 'human' is omitted. The manual's Earth-bound Metroid line was verified ('were bringing it back to Earth when it was stolen by the space pirates'). The Metroid Wiki Earth stub's claim that HQ is on Earth was excluded.

entries.comment: Samus: Exotic materials: Cordite, Bendezium, Denzium, Talloric Alloy, Brinstone, Radion and Urithic Ore
entries.content:
Samus Aran's suit scans rate the dense substances she meets by the weapon that breaks them.

- Cordite: a durable material the Chozo built with throughout their Tallon IV settlements, carved into statues and wall hangings that often conceal Power Conduits or Runic Symbols; a Super Missile breaks it. The Space Pirates adopted it too: a Phazon Mines terminal logged steel hatch covers being "replaced with Cordite and Bendezium covers in two deca-cycles."
- Bendezium: an extremely dense material found naturally on Tallon IV and used extensively by its Chozo colonists. Only a high-yield blast such as a Power Bomb destroys it, though water supersaturation and microfractures weaken it. Samus met it in the Warrior Shrine and Shore Tunnel of Magmoor Caverns and at Phazon Mines gates such as Security Access A.
- Denzium: a strong alloy on Aether and Dark Aether, akin to Bendezium and likewise broken only by Power Bombs. Per O-Lir, last Sentinel of the Fortress Temple, the mechanical sentinels he built, later corrupted by the Ing, fashioned it to block key areas.
- Talloric Alloy: a common material in drain covers, grates and tunnel caps on Tallon IV, Aether and Bryyo, used by Federation, Pirate, Chozo and Bryyonian builders alike; one Morph Ball Bomb breaks a cracked piece.
- Brinstone and Radion: substances Missiles shatter. Brinstone formed a wall, a Chozo shaman bust and pillars on Tallon IV; a wall section, pillars and a statue on Aether and Dark Aether; and a weathered cliffside on Bryyo. Radion is rare, found only twice in Phendrana Drifts: a grating made brittle by temperature swings, and the casing of fuel cells at a tower's base whose destruction opened the way to the Artifact of Elder.
- Urithic Ore: the primary mineral of Zebes's crust; planetary records (spelling it Urthic) call it ideal for subterranean construction.
entries.notes: Each material is sourced to its Metroid Wiki page and scan data. Nits applied from the fact-check: Cordite now 'often conceal Power Conduits or Runic Symbols' (the wiki's general prose); the Bendezium locations were narrowed to the scanned Warrior Shrine, Shore Tunnel and Security Access A; Brinstone was corrected against the re-read Brinstone page (Tallon IV: Ruined Gallery wall, Chozo Ice Temple shaman bust, Tower of Light pillars; Aether: one Sand Processing half-pipe section, Mining Station A and Mining Plaza pillars, a Doomed Entry statue; Bryyo: the Hidden Court cliffside); O-Lir's title is now 'last Sentinel of the Fortress Temple'. Trimmed toward about 300 words by cutting the Pirate-lab location list and the Elite Pirate stasis-tank aside. The Phazon Mines terminal quote is verbatim. The Talloric Alloy multi-builder claim is supported by the G.F.S. Theseus Morph Ball hatch on Bryyo. Metroid Wiki has no Urithic Ore page; both spellings are keys. Weapon mechanics live in the Equipment entries. Order 90 (index-type). 'Cordite' is also a real propellant; that misfire risk was accepted as harmless.
